Definition: properly, to scrape (literally, to shave; but usually figuratively) together (i.e. to accumulate or increase) or away (i.e. to scatter, remove, or ruin; intransitively, to perish)
BiblicalUsage: The Old Testament word çâphâh means to scrape together, or to scatter and ruin. It appears 20 times, and the passages that use it — 1 Chronicles and 1 Samuel among them — show it in its natural setting. Read them together and the meaning settles itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God chose çâphâh on purpose. To scrape together, or to scatter and ruin is not an accident of language; it is the way He says what He means.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
